alt: Five Section A plays grouped by playwright: Othello, King Lear and Hamlet by Shakespeare, Doctor Faustus (B text) by Marlowe, and The Duchess of Malfi by Webster. The passage is printed on the paper; the rest of the play must come from memory. A timeline shows the A text of Doctor Faustus printed in 1604 and the longer B text, the one the specification names, printed in 1616.
caption: One play, one printed passage, and everything else from memory.

after: ## The aspects of tragedy a passage can open up
alt: A hub labelled the passage links to seven aspects of tragedy suggested by the specification: the protagonist’s journey towards death, the villain or opponent in a contest of power, fate, structure from order to disorder, plots and sub-plots, dramatic language, and the audience moved through pity and fear. A note says the absence of an aspect can be as significant as its presence.
caption: Seven productive aspects, and the absence of one can matter as much.

after: ## Reading the passage: a four-step method
alt: A falling curve runs from order through complication to catastrophe. An early passage near the start usually sets up the flaw or the contest of power; a late passage near the end usually shows recognition, suffering or catastrophe.
caption: Where the passage falls in the arc shapes what it is likely to show.

after: ## Reading the passage: a four-step method
alt: Four numbered steps: place the passage in the tragic arc, read the dramatic method closely, name the aspect of tragedy at stake, and reach outward to at least two other moments. Below, an observation that Iago speaks in prose becomes analysis when it explains how his plain prose helps the villain win the contest of power.
caption: Name the tragic aspect each method serves, then reach out to the rest of the play.

alt: A table of five contexts: revenge tragedy conventions for Hamlet and The Duchess of Malfi, the morality-play tradition for Doctor Faustus, the fall of the great for King Lear and Othello, ideas of order for The Duchess of Malfi and King Lear, and performance conditions such as boy actors and a bare stage.
caption: Each context earns credit only when it changes how a specific line reads.

after: ## Worked example on an original passage
alt: Four details of the original Jacobean-style passage are linked to the model paragraph’s analysis: the contradictory candle orders (insight), the hand that once held a sword but has learned the trick of signing deaths (the fall from prosperity), the embedded stage direction as he studies his hand, and the shared line Let them wait. Below, the paragraph ends on the audience’s pity, and with a real play would also link to other moments.
caption: Two tragic aspects, four methods, and an ending on the audience’s response.
